findings.summary: ActionScript is an object-oriented scripting language originally created for Adobe Flash, now implemented as a variant of ECMAScript (JavaScript). It evolved from simple frame commands into a full programming language supporting classes, events, and 3D graphics. Versions 2 and 3 differ in typing and performance, with AS3 using a just-in-time compiler and AVM2 virtual machine for significant speed improvements. The language is used for web animations, rich applications, desktop software via AIR, and game UI elements.

mechanisms.title: Compilation to bytecode and virtual machine execution
mechanisms.explanation: ActionScript code is compiled into bytecode and executed by a virtual machine. ActionScript 1 and 2 run on AVM1, while ActionScript 3 uses the rewritten AVM2 with a just-in-time compiler for faster performance.

mechanisms.title: Event-driven programming model
mechanisms.explanation: The language uses an event-handling model to manage user interactions, media, and system events. This model was expanded in later Flash Player versions to support complex application logic and multimedia control.
